note: Goyon's own 1978 resurvey of the north-east arris, independent of Petrie's Plate VIII. The course table on pp. 410–413 is headed "Hauteur successive en centimètres de toutes les assises de la Grande Pyramide, prises sur l'angle Nord-Est en partant du bas (au-dessus du socle)": 201 courses from the bottom, the 201st the summit platform, courses 1 and 2 counted by the French Expedition rather than by Goyon, each reading good to 0.5 cm, totalling 138.745 m at a mean course of 0.690 m. Every page of the IFAO scan is stamped "© IFAO", so the PDF is not kept in the repository and only the numbers are here. The scan is an image and cannot be read by machine, so scripts/courses.ts imports the table from the transcription on French Wikipedia, "Mesure des rangs d'assises de la pyramide de Khéops" (https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesure_des_rangs_d%27assises_de_la_pyramide_de_Kh%C3%A9ops), revision 230669445, whose wikitext has sha256 9d3f16b06b04c7cdb52ea837d726a46d7a47cad3dd170f6890faac87674600cc. That transcription is CC BY-SA 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/; the 201 heights themselves are Goyon's measurements and are cited to him. It was checked against the scan course by course for courses 1 to 48 and in samples beyond, and the import re-checks Goyon's own two totals on every run.

citation: Commonly cited WGS84 coordinates of three points on the Nile Delta: the Delta Barrage at El-Qanater el-Khayreya, where the river divides (30°11′ N, 31°08′ E); Alexandria (31°12′ N, 29°55′ E); and Port Said (31°15′ N, 32°18′ E).
note: Placeholders, and placeholders of a second kind: not only are the positions uncited gazetteer values, the places themselves stand in for features Stecchini's claim is actually about. Alexandria and Port Said are modern towns standing for the Canopic and Pelusiac mouths, the Delta's western and eastern limits in antiquity, and the barrage is a nineteenth-century dam standing for the head of the Delta. Every one of them is a town or a structure rather than a point, so each is quoted to the arcminute and entered with a sigma of 0.02°, about 2 km. Stecchini's own figures, an axis of Egypt at 31°14′ E and a Delta apex at 30°06′ N, reach us only through Tompkins' appendix and secondary accounts of it, and are not entered.

citation: Commonly cited WGS84 coordinates of the Great Sphinx of Giza: 29°58′31″ N, 31°08′16″ E.
note: Placeholder until a position tied to the ARCE Sphinx Project or the GPMP grid is entered. The figure is what gazetteers and map services give for the monument as a whole rather than a surveyed point on it, and none of them states which point of the statue it is or, in most cases, which datum. The Sphinx is about 450 m from the Great Pyramid's base centre, so at this accuracy the bearing from it to anything on the plateau is good to a degree or so and no better.

Required attribution: HYG Database v4.2 by astronexus, https://codeberg.org/astronexus/hyg, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. data/stars/hyg-bright.json and data/stars/named.json are adapted databases under that licence and carry the credit in their own headers.
note: HYG moved off github.com/astronexus/HYG-Database, which stops at v4.1 and points here. On Codeberg the file is stored with Git LFS, so the /media/ URL above returns the 13 MB gzip and the /raw/ one returns only the 133-byte pointer; sha256 of the gzip is 5ca9431ff364c8002a4a3efa91b2b9296746aea1543374db4cb6b4fab049d601 and the version is dated 2025-06-29 by its own gzip timestamp. HYG gives right ascension in hours and distance in parsecs; scripts/stars.ts converts both and cuts the catalogue to magnitude 6.5. Row 0 of the CSV is the Sun, at right ascension 0 and distance 0, and is dropped. A distance of 100000 pc or more is HYG marking a missing or negative Hipparcos parallax.
